name: transliteration
doc:
TRANSLITERATION - romanizing the original tongue (Matt, 2026-10-10: comprehensive linguistics,
step 2). A Greek word maps by a fixed deterministic scheme to Latin letters; a claimed
romanization is SEALED through linguistics.LING_VERIFY. Greek only (it writes its vowels);
Hebrew declines pending vowel pointing. Idempotent.

marks.claim: [Greek -> Latin, SEALED] 'logos' (lambda-omicron-gamma-omicron-sigma) romanizes by a fixed scheme (eta->e, omega->o, upsilon->y, breathing stripped), sealed through linguistics.LING_VERIFY. The romanization is deterministic: a wrong claim can never match.

[0 false positives, honest about scheme] The check CONFIRMS only an exact match to the engine's scheme; a DIFFERENT valid romanization is a mismatch against THIS scheme, not a false claim, and the verdict says so. Hebrew DECLINES - its romanization depends on vowel pointing that running text omits.

[on the one map - comprehensive linguistics, step 2] Transliteration broadens the linguistics domain BEYOND Strong's: a general romanizer, not only a lexicon lookup. It rests on the linguistics floor (card_floor_indo_european) with phonology, morphology and etymology; semantic relations and closed-class POS are next.
